name: Killymoon Creek
description:
Sunday, 27th April
Killymoon Creek
Led by Molly Hoey


Killymoon Creek, 
Bowling Green Bay NP

Led by Molly Hoey 


Level - Beginner friendly, off track, creek hopping

Where to Meet:

7 am - will advise via email to those that have RSVPd. 

Walk Description:

Killymoon Creek, in the dry season, is a fantastic spot for rock-hopping enthusiasts. This walk start on a fire trail on private property with a few good hills to get everyone warmed up. The creek bed starts as a series of small rocky gullies which soon open up into a spectacular gorge.

We will take lunch at the swimming hole, where the polar bears amongst us can have a dip before lunch. This will be our turn around point and we will descend back down the creek from here.

This adventure will see us tackling numerous kinds of climbing. You will need to have a suitable level of fitness and coordination.

How long:

Full day walk. Estimate back at the car park around 4 pm.

What to bring:

Advised equipment: Water (at least 4L as we cannot guarantee suitable water from the creek), Lunch (Snacks and electrolytes), Basic first aid, suitable sun safe clothing, sun screen, Mozzie spray and suitable shoes.

Speciality equipment: I strongly advise gloves as this walk requires a lots of hand work (but that’s just personal preference). You will need boots with plenty of tread for grip.


RSVP 

To RSVP, please get in touch with Molly Hoey - molly.hoey1@gmail.com. 

Non-members/Guests = $5 club fee to participate.

name: Hidden Valley
description:
Hidden Valley explore
Leader Luen Warneke
Date 18th-20th Apr 2025

Join us for a memorable bushwalking club adventure over the Easter break (18–20 April 2025) exploring the fascinating history and natural beauty of the Hidden Valley and Kangaroo Hills areas in North Queensland.

Set up camp in a serene, sandy creek location where water is readily available for swimming and relaxation. Our base will serve as the ideal starting point for daily short hikes to historical mining sites and remnants of once-thriving townships. Wander through landscapes dotted with historic artefacts, old machinery, and mining infrastructure, providing a vivid insight into Queensland’s rich mining past.

Each day offers a leisurely walk to different points of interest. Visit old mine shafts, tunnels, and discover colourful copper-bearing rocks, historic vehicles, and machinery. Experience a slice of history first-hand and gain a deeper understanding of the region’s early mining days.

We may also venture to explore nearby areas, including picturesque Wallaroo Gorge and Running River Gorge. These properties offer opportunities for exploration, featuring mini-gorges, beautiful creeks, waterfalls, and scenic bushland. Expect to immerse yourself in the tranquility of these secluded and historically significant locations.

Note: The hikes are rated easy to moderate. All hikes are short, day-based excursions, allowing ample time to relax at the campsite. Prior permissions for accessing private properties have been organised for the group.

RSVP early to secure your spot for a weekend filled with adventure, history, and nature. Please ensure you have all camping essentials, including sufficient food, water, and camping gear.

Contact Luen Warneke at luenwarneke@gmail.com or the Townsville Bushwalking Club at info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.com.au for further details or to RSVP.

name: Antill Plains Creek
description:
Saturday, 12th April
Anthill Plains Creek - 
Led by Luen Warneke

Antill Plains Creek Tributary – Rock Hop & Swim Adventure [Bowling Green Bay NP]
 Grade: Level 5- Strenuous, off-track, rock-hopping, variable terrain. This walk will be suitable for experienced bushwalkers. 
 Distance: Flexible  - approx. 14 km return ( route dependant)
 Estimated time: 6-9 hours
 Leader: Luen Warneke
 Start point: Participants will be notified via email 

Meeting Time : 6:30 am 
Overview:
This is an off-track, exploratory-style bushwalk following the tributary of Antill Plains Creek -  a rugged and rewarding slice of Bowling Green Bay National Park. Think granite boulders, creeklines, and pristine swim spots. 
It’s a choose-your-own-adventure kind of day: we’ll head upstream, rock-hop our way toward one or more waterfalls, and cool off in one of the stunning swimming holes along the way.
We’re not heading to Joy’s Cliff this time, but if the group is fast and we make good time, this might be an option. Otherwise, that’s an epic for another day. This walk is all about tuning into the terrain, reading the group, and making decisions as we go. If the going is slow or the vibe is chill, we’ll stop at the first major cascade for a well-earned swim and return the same way. If we’re all bounding along like gazelles, we might continue further upstream or even take a return route via the adjacent ridge or neighbouring creek.

Important Notes:
This walk is weather dependent – wet rocks = high slip risk = alternate plan


Solid bushwalking fitness and confidence on uneven terrain are essential


Bring 3-4 L water, hat, snacks/lunch, first aid kit, and swimmers/towel.  You can fill up at creeks, however the club advises the use of water purification tablets. 


Grippy footwear is a must – boots or trail shoes with good tread. You are likely to get wet feet, so be prepared. We will not be stopping to remove and re-wear our boots. 


This is a remote, unmarked walk – come prepared for a full day out


RSVP 
Fee: non-members/visitors/-  $5 . TBWC Club members - Free.
Everyone welcome on this walk - You can become a TBWC member after 3 walks as a visitor

 
IMPORTANT - If you have not walked with the club before - please get in touch with the walk leader to discuss suitability, before you RSVP

To RSVP, please contact Luen Warneke - luenwarneke@gmail.com
